GNU coreutils 8.32: cat comm cut date fold head join md5sum paste seq shuf sort tail tee tr uniq wc
Licence: GPL-3.0-or-later (COPYING and LICENSE in this folder)
Upstream source: https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/coreutils/coreutils-8.32.tar.xz
  (a copy is in ../../../licenses/sources/, with the build recipe in ../../../licenses/biowasm-build/)
WebAssembly build: Biowasm (https://biowasm.com/), downloaded from
  https://biowasm.com/cdn/v3/coreutils/8.32/ on 2026-09-30 (fold, shuf: 2026-10-01; md5sum, date: 2026-10-02)
Build recipes: https://github.com/biowasm/biowasm (a pinned copy is in ../../../licenses/biowasm-build/)

Local changes

1. JavaScript loaders (all 17 NAME.js files): exit(status) is recorded as Module.__exitStatus, so
   that the terminal of the practical keeps the exit status of a failed command.

2. WebAssembly programs (all 17 NAME.wasm files): ONE BYTE of each file is changed, which makes the
   C library's stdout unbuffered. As built, these programs lose output that does not end with a
   newline (seq 3 | tr '\n' ' ' printed nothing; head -c 100 FILE dropped the last, unfinished
   line): they flush stdout in a function registered with atexit(), and the builds are linked
   without EXIT_RUNTIME, so that function never runs. The change sets buf_size of the C library's
   stdout object in the program's initial memory from 1024 to 0, exactly as it is for stderr.
   Nothing else is changed and each file keeps its size. The script that makes the change, and
   that can check a file, is ../../../licenses/local-patches/unbuffer-stdout.py
   (applied as: unbuffer-stdout.py *.wasm).
   After the change the output of these programs was compared with native GNU coreutils on
   the command lines of a test of the practical "AI agents for bioinformatics", whose terminal
   this practical shares (test/t_partial.py there): the same, character for character.

3. One loader, date.js: the day of the year (tm_yday in the C library's localtime and mktime) is the
   number of days between the two calendar dates. As downloaded, the loader worked it out from the
   milliseconds since 1 January, local time – one hour short in summer time, so that for a local time
   between 00:00 and 00:59 on a summer day it was the day before, and "date -d 2024-07-15" printed
   "invalid date" in the UK and in Europe. The script is ../../../licenses/local-patches/fix-day-of-year.py
   (applied as: fix-day-of-year.py date.js; one place).

SHA256SUMS lists the files as they are here (after these changes).
